title: Interplay of diffusive and active motion governs cohesin extrusion and CTCF barrier function.
authors: Tortora, Maxime M C; Fudenberg, Geoffrey
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该文用跳-扩散模型描述cohesin介导的DNA环挤压与CTCF屏障功能，属广义蛋白-DNA互作动态机制建模，但对象非TF-DNA体系，方法为物理理论建模而非AI/MD，故为中档匹配。
abstract: Cohesin-mediated loop extrusion constitutes a crucial process for the regulation of chromosome folding and gene expression. A rapidly-growing body of in vitro experiments suggests that cohesin molecular motor activity is finely modulated by both chemical and mechanical cues, whose interplay holds important implications in living cells for development and disease. Yet, biophysical models capable of accurately and efficiently capturing the breadth of reported cohesin behaviors, along with their impacts on DNA spatio-temporal organisation, remain lacking. Here, building on multiple experimental observations of single-cohesin dynamics, we introduce a mesoscale description of cohesin based on the general framework of jump-diffusion processes. We show that the finite stall force of cohesin naturally emerges from the conjunction of active, directional extrusion moves with passive, stochastic drift. The tension-dependent competition between these two orthogonal modes of motion gives rise to highly-heterogeneous cohesin kinetics featuring extrusion, translocation, and loop slipping phases, as observed in vitro . These behaviors are predicted to depend sensitively on both buffer composition and nucleosomal content, reconciling the surprising variability of cohesin kinetics reported across experimental conditions. This jump-diffusion model (JDM) is fully parametrized using available single-molecule measurements and bridges the timescale gap between microscopic stepping events and cohesin regulator association, thus providing mechanistic insights into how CTCF impedes extrusion. Hence, the JDM quantitatively describes force-dependent extrusion in both DNA curtain assays in vitro and in the context of native chromatin for genome folding predictions in nucleo , bridging these previously disparate contexts under a unified numerical and theoretical formalism. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Cohesin folds chromosomes into loops that help regulate gene expression, yet its diverse behaviors and sensitivity to mechanical forces remain largely unexplained. Here, we develop a theory for how competition between active DNA capture and passive sliding governs loop growth, shrinkage, and motion. This framework reconciles seemingly conflicting experimental observations, and predicts how weak forces generated by cohesin on naked DNA in vitro translate into tensions strong enough to drive large-scale genome folding on native chromatin. Jointly considering cohesin mechanics and biochemistry further enables us to explain how the DNA-binding protein CTCF modulates extrusion activity. By connecting single-molecule measurements with chromosome organization mechanisms, we thus provide a quantitative foundation for how physical conditions and regulatory proteins collectively shape genome folding.
abstract_zh: 黏连蛋白介导的环挤压构成了染色体折叠和基因表达调控的关键过程。快速增长的体外实验证据表明，黏连蛋白分子马达活性受到化学和机械线索的精细调控，二者的相互作用在活细胞中对发育和疾病具有重要影响。然而，能够准确且高效地捕捉已报道的黏连蛋白行为多样性及其对DNA时空组织影响的双物理模型仍然缺乏。在此，基于对单黏连蛋白动力学的多项实验观察，我们引入了一种基于跳跃-扩散过程一般框架的黏连蛋白介观描述。我们表明，黏连蛋白的有限失速力自然源于主动定向挤压运动与被动随机漂移的结合。这两种正交运动模式之间的张力依赖性竞争产生了高度异质的黏连蛋白动力学，其特征包括挤压、易位和环滑移阶段，正如体外实验所观察到的。这些行为被预测对缓冲液组成和核小体含量均敏感，从而调和了不同实验条件下报道的黏连蛋白动力学令人惊讶的变异性。该跳跃-扩散模型（JDM）利用现有的单分子测量数据完全参数化，并弥合了微观步进事件与黏连蛋白调节因子结合之间的时间尺度差距，从而为CTCF如何阻碍挤压提供了机制性见解。因此，JDM定量描述了体外DNA curtain实验以及天然染色质背景下核内基因组折叠预测中的力依赖性挤压，将先前这些不同的情境统一在数值和理论形式框架下。意义声明：黏连蛋白将染色体折叠成环，有助于调控基因表达，但其多样化的行为和对机械力的敏感性在很大程度上仍未得到解释。在此，我们发展了一种理论，阐述主动DNA捕获与被动滑动之间的竞争如何调控环的生长、收缩和运动。该框架调和了看似矛盾的实验观察，并预测了体外裸DNA上黏连蛋白产生的弱力如何转化为足以驱动天然染色质上大规模基因组折叠的张力。联合考虑黏连蛋白的力学和生物化学特性，进一步使我们能够解释DNA结合蛋白CTCF如何调节挤压活性。通过连接单分子测量与染色体组织机制，我们为物理条件和调控蛋白如何共同塑造基因组折叠提供了定量基础。
